notes.bp: A screening system for vocal-cord disorders should use continuous Mandarin speech, where the diagnostic evidence is spread across many phonemes rather than one carefully chosen sound.
notes.wh: Some phonemes reveal laryngeal behavior more clearly than others, but selecting them from the speech signal can also make the classifier depend on speaker, text, or recording conditions.
notes.naive: Average the whole utterance or use a fixed phoneme list and assume every segment contributes equally.
notes.ap: Use phonetic posteriorgrams to identify informative phoneme segments, then classify vocal-cord disorders from the selected evidence.
notes.mech: The paper proposes phonetic-posteriorgram-based phoneme selection for vocal-cord-disorder classification in continuous Mandarin speech.
notes.math: The recognizer supplies a soft map from sound to phonetic identity; selection makes the diagnostic model focus on the speech units that expose the relevant production difference.
notes.ww: The paper reports classification results for the selected phonetic evidence on continuous Mandarin speech.
notes.limits: Cohort, disorder labels, language, transcript quality, phoneme selection, and recording conditions limit clinical generalization; classification is not diagnosis.
notes.title: Phonetic Posteriorgram-Based Phoneme Selection for Vocal Cord Disorder Classification in Continuous Mandarin Speech

notes.bp: A deepfake detector should trace and attribute new attack sources, including attacks not represented in training, rather than only say real or fake.
notes.wh: Open-set attacks change synthesis methods and acoustic traces; a dataset can accidentally reward memorizing a generator or speaker instead of identifying source behavior.
notes.naive: Train a closed-set binary classifier and evaluate it only on familiar fake types.
notes.ap: Build systematic variations of deepfake audio with source labels and evaluate open-set detection, tracing, and attribution separately.
notes.mech: STOPA is a dataset of systematic variation of deepfake audio for open-set source tracing and attribution.
notes.math: The task is a structured forensic inference problem: detection asks whether an item is fake, while tracing asks which generating process explains it under variation.
notes.ww: The paper reports dataset resources and benchmark behavior for open-set deepfake source tracing and attribution.
notes.limits: Generator coverage, perturbations, speakers, labels, and open-set split design bound the result; benchmark attribution is not courtroom-grade provenance.
notes.title: STOPA: A Dataset of Systematic VariaTion Of DeePfake Audio for Open-Set Source Tracing and Attribution

notes.bp: A new speech deepfake attack may appear with only a few labeled examples, so detection must adapt without retraining a large model from scratch.
notes.wh: Few examples make neural updates unstable, while the new attack may occupy a different part of acoustic space from old attacks.
notes.naive: Fine-tune all parameters on the few examples or use a fixed detector and accept failure on the new attack.
notes.ap: Use Gaussian-process adaptation to express uncertainty and update the detector from scarce examples.
notes.mech: The paper studies few-shot adaptation for speech deepfake detection with Gaussian processes.
notes.math: The probabilistic adapter separates learning the new attack boundary from pretending that a few examples define it with certainty; uncertainty can guide conservative decisions.
notes.ww: The paper reports few-shot detection adaptation results against the tested baselines.
notes.limits: Attack families, kernel choices, calibration, shots, and base detector limit generalization; uncertainty estimates are not automatically reliable under distribution shift.
notes.title: Few-Shot Speech Deepfake Detection Adaptation with Gaussian Processes

notes.bp: Spoken dialogue state tracking needs training data that sounds like spoken interaction, not only written dialogue that has been read aloud.
notes.wh: Written and spoken styles differ in disfluency, brevity, repair, and turn structure; an LLM rewrite can add plausible language while changing the dialogue-state labels.
notes.naive: Use written dialogue directly or generate paraphrases without checking whether the state remains unchanged.
notes.ap: Use an LLM to transform written dialogue into spoken style while preserving state annotations, then test the resulting data for spoken dialogue-state tracking.
notes.mech: The paper leverages LLMs for written-to-spoken style transformation to enhance spoken dialogue-state tracking.
notes.math: The transformation is constrained paraphrasing: surface form changes, but the underlying user goal and slot state must remain invariant for the data to be useful.
notes.ww: The paper reports spoken dialogue-state-tracking gains from the transformed data.
notes.limits: LLM prompt, domains, state schema, speech realization, annotation checks, and evaluation distribution limit the result; style conversion can silently change intent.
notes.title: Leveraging LLMs for Written to Spoken Style Data Transformation to Enhance Spoken Dialog State Tracking

notes.bp: A neural speech codec should preserve high-quality speech while using visual information when available, and it should fail gracefully when that information is absent.
notes.wh: Video can disambiguate speech and improve reconstruction, but synchronization, bitrate, and privacy make it a conditional source rather than a free improvement.
notes.naive: Encode only audio at a high bitrate or concatenate video features without modeling their timing and reliability.
notes.ap: Integrate visual cues into a high-quality neural speech coder and measure quality, rate, and behavior across audio-visual conditions.
notes.mech: The paper presents a vision-integrated high-quality neural speech coding system.
notes.math: Coding becomes cross-modal reconstruction: the decoder uses synchronized visual evidence to fill or protect acoustic detail while the rate constraint limits what can be transmitted.
notes.ww: The paper reports high-quality neural coding results for the tested audio-visual conditions.
notes.limits: Video quality, synchronization, speakers, bitrate, decoder, and missing-video behavior bound the claim; visual assistance can introduce privacy and spoofing risks.
notes.title: Vision-Integrated High-Quality Neural Speech Coding

notes.bp: Fongbe-to-French speech translation needs a benchmark and models that reflect the language rather than treating the low-resource direction as an afterthought.
notes.wh: Speech translation compounds transcription and translation errors, while limited speakers, orthography, and parallel data make evaluation noisy.
notes.naive: Translate a few examples with a multilingual model and compare scores without documenting the corpus or split.
notes.ap: Extend the Fongbe-French speech-translation corpus, document resources and splits, and establish models and baselines for the direction.
notes.mech: The paper extends the Fongbe-to-French speech translation corpus and presents resources, models, and a benchmark.
notes.math: Resource creation and modeling are one research object: a stable corpus fixes what progress means and reveals where transfer from high-resource languages fails.
notes.ww: The paper reports corpus additions, baseline models, and benchmark results for Fongbe-to-French speech translation.
notes.limits: Corpus size, speakers, alignment, transcription, translation references, and split design bound generalization to Fongbe communities and other low-resource pairs.
notes.title: Extending the Fongbe to French Speech Translation Corpus:  resources, models and benchmark

notes.bp: An audio-aware language model should say when spoken input does not contain enough evidence instead of confidently inventing what it did not hear.
notes.wh: Hallucinations can arise from the language model's prior or from ambiguous/noisy audio; ordinary positive examples do not teach the model when to abstain.
notes.naive: Train only on correct audio-text pairs or add generic negative text and assume the model learns auditory limits.
notes.ap: Synthesize negative samples that explicitly represent what the audio does not contain and train the model to distinguish heard evidence from plausible language completion.
notes.mech: The paper teaches audio-aware large language models what they do not hear through synthesized negative samples.
notes.math: The negative examples define an evidence boundary: language generation is rewarded only when its claim is supported by the acoustic input, not merely likely in context.
notes.ww: The paper reports reduced hallucination behavior for the tested audio-aware models and synthesized negative-sample strategy.
notes.limits: Negative-sample construction, audio quality, prompts, model family, and evaluation rubric limit the claim; abstention quality is not the same as factual clinical reliability.
notes.title: Teaching Audio-Aware Large Language Models What Does Not Hear: Mitigating Hallucinations through Synthesized Negative Samples

notes.bp: A monaural speech synthesizer should produce a binaural signal with believable spatial cues even when it has never seen a paired example for the target speaker.
notes.wh: Binaural cues depend on source position, room, head-related filtering, and speaker content; zero-shot synthesis must infer them without memorizing a fixed room or voice.
notes.naive: Duplicate mono audio into both channels or apply one generic stereo widening effect.
notes.ap: Condition zero-shot speech synthesis on spatial information and generate the two channels with consistent content and interaural cues.
notes.mech: The paper studies zero-shot mono-to-binaural speech synthesis.
notes.math: Spatialization is a structured transformation: linguistic content should remain common across channels while timing and spectral differences encode position and acoustic scene.
notes.ww: The paper reports objective and perceptual results for zero-shot mono-to-binaural synthesis.
notes.limits: Room and position range, speaker diversity, spatial labels, head-related filtering, and listening protocol bound generalization; stereo plausibility is not physical localization accuracy.
notes.title: Zero-Shot Mono-to-Binaural Speech Synthesis
